person.persName: gro lung pa blo gros 'byung gnas
person.note:
On the dates ca. 1040 to 1120, see [HCLRANG3]. This conflicts with a mention, in the Chos 'byung mkhas pa'i dga' ston, of Gro lung pa being considered for serving as abbot after rNam par ba (ID:6147), i.e. in 1151 ([7FZ3B926]: 111). It also makes it difficult that he was a teacher of Phywa pa (ID:3831), which would have been when Phywa pa was 11 years of age or younger.
In view of the epithet "gro lung pa," he possibly hailed from La stod gro lung (ID:7412) or Gro bo lung (ID:7411).

His dates can be approximated as 1070-1130.
He is possibly the same person as Byang 'chad khyung (ID:6382), as [NA9AMDH6] states that Khyung rin chen grags held Byang 'chad (ID:4416) and taught Sa chen (ID:4205) there ([647FFPZR]: 543). [CJ75QQKN]: 339 (fol. 8a/170a1-3). dMar ston's Zhib mo rdo rje ([RA3FK3BK]: 134 and 137), on the other hand, distinguish the two figures and places Sa chen's studies with Khyung at Nyang stod byang 'chad, and those with Khyung rin chen grags at Nyang stod.
On the reference to Khyung as "slang pa/slang pha/slang pha ba" (understood as a regionalism for "glang pa/glang pha ba," see [WL39GVT5]: 940.

person.persName: zul phul bya 'dul ba 'dzin pa chen po
person.note: Born in 1091 at gTsang rong gyung and died at the age of 76 in Zul phu according to [R894SIKE]: 109. [W4T5ZMUP]: 38 accordingly proposes the dates 1091-1166. [VKBZTBWN], fol. 3b6 reports that he was born the year rNgog lo (ID:3786) came back to Tibet, i.e., ca. 1092. On his life, based on the Zul phu mkhan byang chub rin chen dpal bzang po'i rnam par thar pa (ID:6715), see [W4T5ZMUP]: 40. It is unclear whether he is the same person as rGya 'dul ba 'dzin pa (ID:4193). The [NA9AMDH6] distinguishes two "rGya 'dul 'dzin" - the elder (ID: 3941) and the younger (ID:4193) - and a "Bya 'dul 'dzin brTson 'grus 'bar" (student of 'Bre chen po). In contrast, the [R894SIKE] only mentions one "rGya 'dul 'dzin" (the elder), distinct from "Bya 'dul 'dzin" (who was ordained by 'Bre). [VKBZTBWN], fol. 6b5-6 and [8VLVHDR2], fol. 14b5 report that he was ordained by 'Bre and received from him the name in religion brTson 'grus 'bar. A number of the same teachers are mentioned for rGya 'dul 'dzin the younger and Bya 'dul 'dzin but, for instance, the latter's studies with rGya 'dul 'dzin the older took place when he was a retired abbot, whereas the former's studies with him took place when he was still abbot. Further, rGya 'dul 'dzin the younger became abbot of dGa' ba sdong and Bya 'dul abbot of Zul phu. This suggests they might have been distinct persons.

[MGPRHX73]: 58, n. 24 cites an 18th century work that argues that "gzhon nu tshul khrims" is the real name of 'Dul 'dzin dkar mo (ID:3820) and "shes rab 'bum" that of his student dKar chung ring mo (ID:3821).

person.note:
The majority of the information available on Phya pa has been provided in [EZ5JXHJY] and [8S7FDMCJ]. Summaries of the same are also found in [LQZU66YX]: 37-40, [F4UK2S8P]: 2-3, and [BW9UR427]: 35-36 (in French).
On his birth in 1109, the year of rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786)'s passing, see [TM8DW8WA]: 32-33, [VKBZTBWN]: 4b4-5, and [8GL7ZT7Y]: 15b2-3. On the date of his passing in a "sa mo glang" year, see [R894SIKE]: 400, [VKBZTBWN]: 4b4-5 and 6a5. [95UZA9Y5]: 40/3/5 (reported in [7FZ3B926]: 111 and [MPRU5QUC]: 206) specifies the day "sa mo glang gi lo'i nag pa zla ba nag po'i phyogs kyi tshes brgyad," i.e., on the 23rd of the third month.
A list of his students is provided in [EZ5JXHJY]: 356, based on [MQB8JGAX]: 297/4, [KL9XTQWI]: I, 454, [4YEPFBIB]: 340-341, [8GL7ZT7Y], fol. 15b3, [VKBZTBWN], fol. 4b7-5a4. [FDEWZ2NZ]: 290 also mentions the list of the four "jo sras" from bSod nams dpal's Bla ma rngog pa yab sras rim par byon pa’i rnam thar rin po che’i rgyan gyi phreng ba.
'Gos lo tsa ba lists numerous works composed before Phya pa took the see of gSang phu; these include commentaries and summaries on the Five works of Maitreya, the Pramāṇaviniścaya, the Satyadvayavibhaṅga, Madhyamakālaṃkāra, Madhyamakāloka, and Bodhicaryāvatāra. He mentions having seen these, the Yid kyi mun sel (ID:4503) and summaries on Madhyamaka, as well as (ID:4505) and (ID:5971). See exX0032026-04-2304-02-58 . 'Gos lo tsa ba does not mention any composition dealing with monastic discipline.
Śākya mchog ldan ([TM8DW8WA], 12-13 and 32) mentions a (doubtful) commentary on the Pramāṇavārttika (ID:3772) in addition to the commentary on the Pramāṇaviniścaya, and three summaries (small, intermediate, large), the intermediate one being the Yid kyi mun sel (ID:4503). (Discussed in [EZ5JXHJY]: 357, translated in [8S7FDMCJ]: 59).
Four groups of students are mentioned in Tibetan sources (which do not imply that the members of the respective groups were studying with Phya pa at the same time), with occasional variations:
1) The "Eight Great Lions" (seng chen brgyad). Eight scholars whose names contains the expression "seng ge," likely connoting their expertise in epistemology. The standard list includes gTsang nag pa (ID:3839), Dan 'bag (ID:3840), 'Bru sha (ID:3841), rMa bya (ID:3842), rTsags/rTsegs (ID:4289), Myang/Nyang bran (ID:3844), and gNyal pa/dMyal ma (ID:6679). The eighth one is instead sometimes said to be gTsang pa 'Jam dpal (ID:6336), 'U yug pa (ID:3846), or mTshur ston (DI:4315).
2) The "four sons of noble families" (jo sras mi bzhi) or the "three sons of noble families" (jo sras gsum). They are young noble men of the rNgog (ID:3847), 'Khon (ID:3848), Khu (ID:3849), and gNyos/sMyos (ID:3850). The four are listed in [VKBZTBWN]: 4a7 and [8GL7ZT7Y]: 15b3, whereas on 16a1 the author speaks of "jo sras gsum." The four are also listed by bSod nams dpal, see [FDEWZ2NZ]: 290.
3) The "three wise ones" (shes rab can mi gsum) or "four wise ones" (shes rab can mi bzhi). The threefold-list in [VKBZTBWN]: 5a1 has rKong po (ID:3852), lHo pa sgom gzan (ID:3853), Par bu ba/sPar phu ba (ID:3854). 'Gar dbang grub (ID:3851) is added in the fourfold list, e.g. in [R894SIKE]: 406.
4) The "three accomplished ones" (grub thob mi gsum). These are students who later became famous masters: Dus gsum mkhyen pa (ID:3855), Phag mo gru pa (ID:3856), gSal sto (ID:3857). The third is sometimes replaced by Zhang tshal (ID:6409), or is suggested to be the latter's direct student.

First Karmapa. His birth name was dGe 'phel ([Y6NGTTC6]: 24). His alternative names and epithets are listed in [Y6NGTTC6]: 5 and 27, which also lists the main information on his life found in early sources. Dus gsum mkhyen pa (ID:3855), Sho sgom (ID:3857), and Phag mo gru pa (ID:3856) are known as the "grub thob mi gsum" and as the "khams pa mi gsum." According to Dus gsum mkhyen pa'i rnam thar in Si tu Chos kyi 'byung gnas's Karma kam tshang gser 'phreng (cited in [I58Z22ET]: 408, n. 42), Dus gsum mkhyen became known as one of the "khams pa mi gsum" during his stays in gSang phu (ID:4332) (gsang phur yang bzhugs te | khams pa mi gsum du grags |).

person.persName: dge slong blo gros rgyal mtshan
bcom ldan rigs pa'i ral gri
person.note: On his career, see [KHA9ZVGP]: 3-8. The dates 1227-1305 are known from the biography (see work (ID:7016)) composed by his student bSam gtan bzang po (ID:4005) ([KHA9ZVGP]: 3). His name in religion was Dar ma rgyal mtshan or Chos kyi rgyal mtshan ([FZ6N88AU]: 406) - the name Chos kyi rgyal mtshan is given as his "real name" (mtshan dngos) in a homage by Rong ston ([KM47ZZDJ]: 657 and n. 62). The majority of the colophons of his works name him "bCom ldan ral gri," a few "Rigs/Rig pa’i ral gri" or just "Ral gri." Schwabland's discussion of the variants “Rigs pa” and “Rig pa” does not come to a definite conclusion as to which is the correct spelling ([CTQMVBPR]: 2-3). He was born as the son of a local wealthy headman, the fourth of five sons and his birth is reported to have been foretold by Śākyaśrībhadra (ID:6418) when he was invited by Ral gri's paternal uncle ([KHA9ZVGP]: 3).

Commentary on Śāntarakṣita’s Madhyamakālaṃkāravṛtti (ID:3733), with some references to a “commentator” (ti ka byed) and to numerous anonymous opponents. Like in the commentary on the Satyadvayavibhaṅga (see (ID:5874)), the author uses a question-and-answer style to explain the words of the text. A few lemmas hint to a different translation of the base text. In particular, the verse MA 1 is cited in a version different from the canonical one.
The descriptive title given in the conclusive verses ex006052026-04-2303-27-06 - dbu ma brgyan gyi rtogs sla byis pa'i 'jug ngogs su rnam par phye - resembles the title in the colophon of his commentary on the Madhyamakāloka (see (ID:4482): bde blag du rtogs pa byis pa'i 'jug ngogs (ms: ngos) su sbyar ba).
In the text, Phya pa refers the reader to two of his compositions for the details of the proof of emptiness, which he names "shes rab gsum la 'jug pa" and "'jug ngogs bsdu bar bstan la phab pa" (ex006052026-04-2303-25-27 pointed out in [5ENG67Z7]: 82, n. 22). The second could be his commentary on the Madhyamakāloka (ID:4482) on account of the similarity of title; the first could be the dBu ma de kho na nyid kyi snying po (ID:4486) or a work yet unknown. This means that this commentary on the Madhyamakālaṃkāravṛtti would post-date the other two madhyamaka works, dBu ma de kho na nyid kyi snying po being the earliers as it is mentioned in the commentary on the Madhyamakāloka (ID:4482).
Edition and translation of some portions of the work in [WLWGS439]: appendix and footnotes.

Its composition predates the author's commentary on the Madhyamakāloka (ID:4482), which mentions its title as "de kho na nyid kyi snying po." ((ID:7460), 481-482: 'di rnams kyi don kyi cha ni kho bos de kho na nyid kyi snying por rgya cher gtan la dbab pas 'dir ma spros te | legs par rtogs par 'dod pas de las blta bar bya'o ||) (The passage was identified by Jongbok Yi and is cited in [5ENG67Z7]: 81, n. 9). If the commentary on the Madhyamakāloka (ID:4482) is the "'jug ngogs bsdus bar bstan la phab pa" mentioned in the commentary on the Madhyamakālaṃkāra (ID:4482), then the dBu ma de kho na nyid snying po also predates that work. bibl.note: True

Doxographical presentation of non-Buddhist and Buddhist philosophical schools drawing information from the Tarkajvāla (ID:5586), Prajñāpradīpaṭīkā, Tattvasaṃgraha (ID:7416) (and °pañjikā (ID:7417)) and Madhyamakāvatāra (ID:3726)/(ID:5885). It offers summarized refutation of each of the non-Buddhist systems and of some of the Buddhist systems, and rejection of objections against Madhyamaka. It includes extensive quotes for non-Buddhist systems, and a few citations in the section on Buddhist schools (from the Abhidharmakośa (ID:3761), Madhyamakālaṃkāra (ID:3731), Pramāṇavārttika (ID:3772), Triṃśikā, Mahāyānasaṃgraha (ID:3753) and Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra (ID:3746). See [WLWGS439]: 24–25 for the details. The section on Madhyamaka does not mention the division between svātantrika and prāsaṅgika, but only delves on the division between the non-abiding view and illusionist view with regard to ultimate reality, while on the conventional level, the author refutes madhyamka adopting a system akin to yogācāra and to sautrāntika. A synoptic tables is provided in [WLWGS439]: 23 and [UAHPCR5I]: 69-71.
The structure of the text does not follow a strict sa bcad hierarchy (as found in Phya pa’s other works). A six-fold division (not referred to as “chapters”) structures the six systems that Phya pa distinguishes – five non-Buddhists (vaiṣṇava, śaiva, jaina, sāṃkhya, cārvaka) and the Buddhists (see [WLWGS439]: 22).
This doxography was reported by 'Gos lo tsā ba in the [MQB8JGAX] (as phyi nang gi grub mtha’) and by A khu ching in the Tho yig ([5RXEUKD9], No. 11910: phyi nang gi grub mtha’i rnam bzhag bsdus pa) ([WLWGS439]: 21). Werner points out multiple re-use of Phya pa’s doxography in Klong chen pa (ID:6062)'s Grub mtha' mdzod.

Whether the author is Phya pa Chos kyi seng ge (ID:3831) remains to be confirmed, notably upon systematic comparison with another commentary on the °kārikā titled dGe tshul rnams kyi bslab pa'i rim pa ston pa'i rnam par bshad pa (ID:4511), the colophon of which names the author "chos kyi seng ge" and indicates he was a disciple of Bya 'dul (ID:3818). Other candidates for the authorship, see (ID:6566), Phya pa's students (ID:3844) and (ID:3853).
The expression bu ta / 'bu ta is frequently used instead of sangs rgyas (pa). Numerous references to anonymous other thinkers.

bibl.title: dge tshul rnams kyi bslab pa'i rim pa ston pa'i rnam par bshad pa
དགེ་ཚུལ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་བསླབ་པའི་རིམ་པ་སྟོན་པའི་རྣམ་པར་བཤད་པ
thams cad yod par smra ba'i dge tshul rnams kyi bslab pa'i rim pa ston pa'i rnam par bshad pa
bibl.author: phywa pa chos kyi seng ge
bibl.note: True

The author is named "chos kyi seng ge" in the colophon, and it is indicated that he was a disciple of Bya 'dul (ID:3818). This supports the identification as Phya pa (ID:3831).
The author refers to the views of unidentified scholars and teachers (slob dpon) as well as those of his own bla ma - ex009042025-12-0113-10-51, ex009042025-12-0113-23-38 - likely Bya 'dul 'dzin (ID:3818), whom he refers to in the colophon ex9042023-09-09-948 . He also quotes views by "blo gros chen po" ex009042025-12-0113-39-04 and "bshes gnyen" ex009042025-12-0113-10-52 .
Whether the author is identical with the "dharma singha" who authored another commentary on the kārikā and a commentary on the kārikāvṛtti - see (ID:5524) and (ID:4509) - deserves further investigation. The present text has large parallels to (ID:5524), which is however more detailed has more frequent mention and refutation of alternative views, but the present text refers to the base text more systematically.

'dul ba suM rgya pa'i Tik chen cha pa chos kyi seng ges mdzad pa

bibl.note: True

The same scholar, identified in the colophon as "dharma singha" (=Tib. chos kyi seng ge) composed this commentary on the Mūlasarvāstivādiśrāmaṇerakārikā (ID:3764) and on the Mūlasarvāstivādiśrāmaṇerakārikāvṛtti (ID:3766), see (ID:4509). He is likely the same person who composed a So thar mdo'i 'grel ba (ID:4507), whose colophon likewise names the author "dharma singha."
Whether the author is Phya pa Chos kyi seng ge (ID:3831) remains to be confirmed, notably upon systematic comparison with another commentary on the °kārikā titled dGe tshul rnams kyi bslab pa'i rim pa ston pa'i rnam par bshad pa (ID:4511), the colophon of which names the author "chos kyi seng ge" and indicates he was a disciple of Bya 'dul (ID:3818). The present work has parallels to (ID:4511), but is more detailed has more frequent mention and refutation of alternative views. However, (ID:4511) refers more systematically to the base text. Parallels with the anonymous (ID:5253) should also be explored further.
Other candidates for the authorship, see (ID:6566), and Phya pa's students (ID:3844) and (ID:3853).

bibl.title: bslab pa kun las btus pa'i don bsdus pa
བསླབ་པ་ཀུན་ལས་བཏུས་པའི་དོན་བསྡུས་པ

bibl.author: phywa pa chos kyi seng ge
bibl.note: True

Topical outline of Śāntideva’s Śikṣāsamuccaya. It gives a hierarchical structure for the base text (with an initial threefold division), to which it refers by means of interlinear notes indicating lemmas of the base text in the Tibetan translation. Only an incomplete instance is extant (ID:6555). The identity of the author as Phya pa (ID:3831) needs to be confirmed, as it could also be Nyang bran Chos kyi seng ge (ID:3884). Both scholars wrote a commentary on the Śikṣāsamuccaya, see work (ID:7053) and work (ID: 6551).
